segments: The Chronography of the Hebrews {OCR? Chronography of Bar Hebraeus}.

It is told
that when this al-Adil was going from Baysan,
he saw a man carrying a burden, walking for an hour
and sitting for an hour to rest.
And he approached him alone and said to him:
"Why are you killing yourself,
O old man? Do not hurry."
And the old man answered:
"Go tell the Sultan
not to hurry;
for if he had not hurried,
I would never have hurried,
nor would I ever have left my home."
And al-Adil was ashamed,
and he left him and went away.
At this time died Prince Bohemond,
and he left a son whose name was Raymond-Roupen,
whom the daughter of Roupen, King of the Armenians, had borne to him.
And while the kingdom was rightfully his,
his uncle grew bold {OCR?} and seized it for himself.
Now Leo, King of the Armenians, the brother of Roupen the Armenian,
because that Frankish Roupen was the son of his brother's daughter,
was zealous and came to Antioch,
and made the Antiochians swear allegiance to him.
He, however, the wretch {OCR?},
when he saw that he was made king,
became arrogant,
and wanted to seize Leo who had made him king,
so that he might rule over Cilicia as well. But the Friars {Frères},
when they learned of the plot,
informed Leo about it,
and he was saved without harm.
And in the year 1515 [of the Greeks],
615 of the Arabs [1218 AD],
the Franks sailed by sea and went against Damietta,
and went up onto the dry land which is called Jizah {OCR? Giza / al-Jizah};
and the river Nile remained between the Franks and Damietta.
Now the Arabs had built a large tower in the middle of the Nile,
so that the warriors in it held back the Franks from Damietta.
And when the Franks fought against that tower for about four months,
they took it,
and killed the men who were in it,
and cut the chains that were across the Nile.
Now al-Malik al-Kamil, the son of al-Adil, was encamped on the other side of Damietta;
and when he saw that the Franks had cut the chains that were across the Nile,
he fastened a great bridge in place of the chains.
And the Franks cut that bridge as well.
Then al-Kamil pierced many large ships and sank them in that place,
so that the large ships could not pass over those sunken ships.
The Franks, however, dug a large and deep trench on the other side,
and breached a breach,
and channeled a large stream from the Nile through that breach,
